english.title: Receive weapon instruction / training - Terrorism Act 2000
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), received instruction or training in

(A)_[the making of]_
(B)_[the use of]_

(C)_[firearms]_
(D)_[explosives]_
(E)_[chemical, biological or nuclear weapons]_
(F)_[radioactive material or weapons designed or adapted for the discharge of any radioactive material]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 54(2) and (6) of the Terrorism Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required
(ii) See Section 54(5) for defence
(iii) See Section 55 for definition of "chemical weapon", "biological weapon" or "nuclear weapon"
(iv) This offence applies to acts done outside the United Kingdom regardless of the nationality of the offender, section 17 of the Terrorism Act 2006.
(v) Option F added by section 120(1) of the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001.
(vi) From 13th April 2015, the maximum sentence was amended from 10 years imprisonment to life imprisonment. This amendment applies only in relation to an offence committed on or after 13th April 2015. Where an offence is found to have been committed over a period of 2 or more days, or at some time during a period of 2 or more days, it must be taken to have been committed on the last of those days.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Life imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited. This offence is also specified as a serious terrorism offence (Part 1 of Schedule 17A to the Sentencing Act 2020) and subject to serious terrorism sentences of imprisonment or extended sentences; see note (v) in section 306 for details.
